message.content:
Black holes form when **gravity overwhelms pressure** in a very dense object, most commonly when a **massive star runs out of fuel** and its core collapses after a supernova or directly into a black hole.[1][2][6][9]

The main formation paths are:

- **Stellar collapse:** A very massive star exhausts its nuclear fuel; its core can no longer support itself, so it collapses. If the remaining core is massive enough, the collapse continues until a black hole forms.[2][4][6][9]
- **Supernova fallback:** In some cases, a star explodes, but enough material falls back onto the core that it becomes a black hole.[1]
- **Mergers:** Black holes can also form when **neutron stars merge** or when smaller black holes merge into larger ones.[1][6]
- **Direct collapse in the early universe:** Some theories say large gas clouds may have collapsed directly into black holes, especially to seed **supermassive black holes**.[1][2][6]
- **Primordial black holes:** A speculative idea is that some black holes formed from extreme density fluctuations shortly after the Big Bang.[1][6]

After formation, a black hole can grow by **accreting gas, stars, or merging with other black holes**.[1][4][7]
